reconstructed_theorem_text: For all natural numbers d,n with 3<=n and n<=d, every real kappa with 4<=kappa, and every family O of real orthogonal n by n matrices indexed by Fin(d div n), define A as follows. Put q = d div n and r = d mod n, with natural-number division and remainder, so d = q*n + r. For each j in {0,...,q-1}, define the real n by n block B_j = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O_j + O_j^T). The resulting real d by d matrix A has q consecutive blocks B_0,...,B_(q-1), followed by I_r, and all entries between distinct blocks or between a main block and the tail are zero. The pair (i,j), with inner coordinate i in {0,...,n-1} and block index j in {0,...,q-1}, maps to coordinate j*n+i. Tail coordinate k in {0,...,r-1} maps to q*n+k. Both row and column indices use this same map (reindexing uses its inverse to retrieve the original entries). If r=0, the tail is empty: I_0 has no entries and adds no coordinates. Define the real-valued potential f on R^d by f(x) = (1/2) x^T A x. Then f(0)=0, and for every x in R^d, f(x)>=0 and (f(x)=0 if and only if x=0). Thus the zero set is exactly {0}; together with nonnegativity and f(0)=0 this says that the global minimum value is 0 and the origin is its unique minimizer. In particular f(x)>0 for every nonzero x.
objects: Natural numbers d,n; real scalar kappa; q=d div n; r=d mod n; an indexed family O_j of real orthogonal n by n matrices; blocks B_j; the reindexed real matrix A; identity matrices I_n and I_r; the coordinate equivalence e from ((Fin n x Fin q) disjoint-union Fin r) to Fin d. The potential f(x)=(1/2)x^T A x, vectors x in R^d, and the zero vector 0.
domains: d,n belong to the natural numbers, including zero where not otherwise restricted; kappa belongs to the real numbers; j belongs to Fin q; inner coordinates belong to Fin n; residual coordinates belong to Fin r; A has rows and columns in Fin d and real entries; O maps Fin q to the real orthogonal group on Fin n. The potential f maps (Fin d -> real) to real; x ranges over all real vectors indexed by Fin d.
quantifiers: For every d,n : natural numbers, if 3<=n and n<=d, then for every kappa : real, if 4<=kappa, then for every orthogonal family O, let A be the displayed matrix and let f(x)=(1/2)x^T A x. The assertion is f(0)=0 and, for every x : Fin d -> real, the conjunction 0<=f(x) and (f(x)=0 iff x=0).
assumptions: 3<=n; n<=d; 4<=kappa; O_j is a real orthogonal n by n matrix for every j in Fin(d div n). No further assumptions on x are imposed.
conclusion: f(0)=0; every x satisfies f(x)>=0; and every x satisfies f(x)=0 exactly when x=0. Consequently the origin is the unique global minimizer and the minimum value is zero; equivalently f is strictly positive off the origin.
scopes: The matrix blocks are ordered by j first and inner coordinate i second: global coordinate j*n+i; the residual tail starts at q*n. The coordinate equivalence is used for both rows and columns. An empty residual set contributes no identity coordinates. A is locally defined from d,n,kappa,O; f is then locally defined from A on all of R^d. Both remain fixed in the universal assertion over x. The iff concerns the whole vector equality x=0, not an individual coordinate or one block.
constant_dependencies: The potential normalization is exactly 1/2. The dimension hypotheses use 3 and the kappa lower bound uses 4. The matrix coefficients are exactly (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4, with an identity tail of coefficient 1. The attained minimum and all zeros are described using the exact scalar 0. There are no unspecified constants or existential choices.
